packageRules.description: Go version: group all Go version updates together to keep them in sync. The go.mod toolchain directive (gomod manager, datasource golang-version) is what CI installs via setup-go, so a Go security release reaches CI through this group; the go directive is a minimum and is not bumped.
Go version: the golang builder image in the Dockerfile moves together with the go.mod toolchain, so the released binaries are built with the minor version CI tests
Bundle golang.org/x/* updates with Go version bumps so a consistent set lands together (e.g. golang.org/x/crypto fixes shipped alongside Go releases)
Go version: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go version: require manual review for major updates
Go modules: enable updates for indirect dependencies so transitive security patches land without waiting for a direct require to bump
Go modules: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go modules: require manual review for major updates on direct requires

Go modules: never open major PRs for indirect deps. Module-path bumps (/v2 -> /v3) cannot be auto-applied without a direct importer, so go mod tidy resets the indirect line to the MVS minimum and Renovate keeps re-opening the same downgrade PR. Major updates land via the parent direct dependency.
Docker base images (non-Go): automerge minor and patch updates
Docker base images: require manual review for major updates
GitHub Actions: automerge minor and patch updates
GitHub Actions: automerge major updates after CI passes
Workflow-pinned tools (custom regex manager, e.g. golangci-lint): automerge minor and patch updates
Workflow-pinned tools (custom regex manager): require manual review for major updates
npm: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
npm: require manual review for major updates

TypeScript is pinned by the Angular toolchain: @angular/compiler-cli and @angular/build declare peerDependency 'typescript >=6.0 <6.1'. Newer TS (e.g. v7) breaks the Angular build, so cap it at Angular's supported upper bound. Widen this when the Angular peerDependency range widens.

Angular framework, CLI/build tooling and Material are released in lockstep and peer-depend on each other: a major update of any of them is one grouped PR. Separate PRs produced half-upgrades (@angular/core 22.2 next to @angular/build 22.1).

Angular minor and patch updates arrive through lock file maintenance, not as their own PRs. npm cannot move the Angular peer set inside an existing lock file: exact peer pins (@angular/compiler-cli -> @angular/compiler, the optional @angular/localize -> @angular/compiler-cli) make the incremental lock file update fail with ERESOLVE, so the Angular CLI update never got a PR. A freshly generated lock file resolves cleanly, and the ^22 ranges in package.json already allow every minor and patch.

conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits v10 is incompatible with @semantic-release/release-notes-generator v14: releases get a heading but no commit sections (empty release notes). Cap at v9 until the semantic-release plugins support the v10 preset API.
Use 'fix' instead of 'chore' for dependency updates
GitHub Actions: use 'chore' instead of 'fix' for updates

Lock file maintenance: regenerate the npm lock files weekly and automerge after CI passes. This carries the Angular minor and patch updates (see above) and keeps transitive versions current: @angular/compiler-cli 22.2 calls an API of @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec 1.6 but declares ^1.4.14, and an incrementally updated lock file kept 1.5.5.

customManagers.description: Update tool versions pinned in GitHub workflows via renovate comments: a `version:` action input (golangci-lint) or a shell variable such as KIND_VERSION on the line below the comment
